office_does: A King County Southwest Electoral District District Court judge hears and decides misdemeanor criminal cases, small claims, traffic cases and protection orders for a four-year term; in practice the discretion is in pretrial release, sentencing, protection orders and therapeutic-court supervision.
race_blurb: Incumbent Judge Fa'amomoi Masaniai, Jr., appointed in 2021 and reprimanded by the Commission on Judicial Conduct in April 2026 over 2023 conduct toward a court clerk, faces Des Moines Councilmember Harry Steinmetz, who reports work as an administrative law judge and whose endorsers include the court's Chief Presiding Judge. The race skipped the primary.

candidates.summary: District Court judge since a 2021 King County Council appointment, assigned to the Regional Mental Health and Veterans Courts since 2023. He came to law through the WSBA Rule 6 clerkship and is Washington's first judge of Samoan heritage.
highlights: Appointed in 2021, elected unopposed in 2022; Regional Mental Health and Veterans Courts since 2023 [S2][S6]
Prosecutor in American Samoa and public defender for Shoreline before the bench, per his campaign and court bio [S2][S7]
Says "Justice is about more than punishment" and favors treatment and job training, while incarcerating repeat offenders if rehabilitation fails [S1][S8]
Reprimanded by the Commission on Judicial Conduct on April 24, 2026, by stipulation, for 2023 conduct toward a court clerk [S4]
Endorsed by three sitting King County District Court judges [S10]

safety.basis: Explicit rehabilitation-and-treatment framing and a therapeutic-court assignment, tempered by his stated readiness to incarcerate repeat offenders.

experience.basis: Sitting judge for about five years (appointed 2021, elected 2022) running for retention on that record.

candidates.summary: Des Moines City Councilmember who reports work as a Board of Industrial Insurance Appeals administrative law judge, pro tem judge, prosecutor and defense attorney. His endorsers include the District Court's Chief Presiding Judge and seven other sitting judges.
highlights: Re-elected to the Des Moines City Council in 2025; Deputy Mayor 2024-25 [S3][S4]
Reports 36 years as an administrative law judge, pro tem judge, prosecutor and defense attorney (self-reported) [S1][S2]
Pamphlet quotes Chief Judge Rebecca Robertson calling him "extraordinarily well qualified" [S1]
Campaigns on judicial conduct "on and off the bench"; his site addresses his opponent's reprimand [S1][S2]

experience.basis: Mixed: a long legal career with administrative-judge, pro tem and elected-council service, but challenging a sitting judge without a trial-court judgeship of his own.
